card.title: For Everyone’s Protection
card.instruction: Protect people by creating procedures for them. Turn concern into checklists, permissions, required steps, and increasingly narrow exceptions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you borrow my bicycle, let's rehearse what to do if you wobble. I don't want you hurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Which foot? I'll tick that side off.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Whichever side I'm falling toward. I need to get to work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll practise both sides separately. Until both are signed off, you can borrow it for walking.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 makes bicycle borrowing conditional on a protective rehearsal, A3 requires side-specific signoff, and A5 narrows permission to walking until both sides pass.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's foot-down answer causes A3's which-foot classification; B4's adaptive answer and work urgency cause A5's two rehearsals and restricted loan.

relationship.evidence: B2 gives a sensible balance response and B4 explains that the side depends on the actual fall.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's flexible competence as grounds for two formal checks rather than permission to ride.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes borrowing a bicycle and an explicit desire to prevent injury.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's walking-only exception follows B4's need to get to work and the unresolved signoffs.
